tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list projects accessible to the connected CronCool account, including identifiers needed to select a project. Returns each project's id, name and creation time, 50 by default and 100 at most, with a flag when more exist. Not for listing jobs.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list scheduled jobs in CronCool to inspect schedules, enabled state and the latest execution status. Returns each job's id, name, schedule, target origin, method, enabled state and last run status and time, 20 per page by default, with a cursor for more. Not for a job

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read the scheduling configuration and latest execution metadata of one CronCool job selected by its exact identifier. Returns the job's name, cron expression, type, target origin, HTTP method, content type, enabled state and last run status and time, or not-found. Not

tools.name: run_job
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to immediately execute the configured request for one CronCool job. Returns only that Croncool invoked it, not the target's response. Each call immediately sends the job's configured request again, which can write, message or bill downstream, and a repeated call sends it

tools.name: get_job_runs
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read execution history for one CronCool job to inspect success, failure, HTTP status and duration. Returns recent runs newest first with success or failure, HTTP status, duration and time (no response bodies), 20 by default and 100 at most. Not for starting a run.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list durable workflow definitions and run-count summaries for one CronCool project. Returns each workflow's name, run counts by status and last run time for one project, 50 by default and 100 at most. Not for individual runs.

tools.name: list_workflow_runs
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list executions of a durable workflow in CronCool, with optional workflow-name and status filters. Returns each run's id, workflow name, status, timings and error code, newest first by default, 20 per page with a cursor, filterable by workflow and status. Not for one

tools.name: get_workflow_run
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read one CronCool workflow execution and a bounded page of its step statuses for troubleshooting. Returns the run's status, timings and error code plus its steps with status, attempt, timings and error code, 50 steps by default and 200 at most. Not for listing runs.

tools.name: list_webhook_subscriptions
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read CronCool webhook subscription configuration and recorded delivery failures. Returns each subscription's endpoint origin, events, active state, consecutive failures, auto-disabled flag and last delivery time, 20 by default. Works only with a signed-in user session

tools.name: open_croncool
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to open the CronCool project-selection sidebar when the user requests an interactive project and job browser. Returns up to 100 projects to start from (no request payloads, workflow bodies, secrets or full target URLs). Not for running jobs or changing their configuratio

tools.name: show_project_overview
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to render a read-only overview of one CronCool project and a bounded preview of its scheduled jobs. Returns an overview card with the project's name and creation time, whether workflow hosting is set up, and up to 12 jobs with schedule, target origin and last run status.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "open_croncool" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: open_croncool · Private data: list_webhook_subscriptions, open_croncool · Public sink: list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_jobs, get_job, run_job, get_job_runs, list_workflows, list_workflow_runs, get_workflow_run, show_project_overview.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: open_croncool · Private data: list_webhook_subscriptions, open_croncool · Public sink: list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_jobs, get_job, run_job, get_job_runs, list_workflows, list_workflow_runs, get_workflow_run, show_project_overview

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
